title: Fynaptix · Space Economy Research
heading: Space Economy Intelligence
subheading: Launch, satellites, constellations & the post-SpaceX-IPO landscape
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Space is capital-intensive with heavy government-customer concentration. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: Global space economy estimated at ~$626B in 2026 and projected to reach $1.8T by 2035; private space-startup funding was last reported at a record $20.3B year to date.

SpaceX closed near $158.96 on Oct 2 after Starship Flight 14 put 26 Starlink V3 satellites in orbit; still above the $135 IPO price but well below the $225.64 52-week high, with up to 1.3B lockup shares unlocking after Q3 earnings.

kpis.sub: ROCKET LAB EQUITY RAISE FOR IRIDIUM
kpis.label: Rocket Lab sold ~29.3M shares at ~$66 (about 5% dilution) and terminated its $3.6B bridge loan; Iridium holders' shares at closing (mid-2027) could lift total dilution to ~12%, and RKLB trades above 40x annualized revenue.
Starlink doubled subscribers year over year to 12.0M with a record 1.7M Q2 net adds, but average revenue per user fell to $66 a month from $85 as the base broadened.

tiers.label: Scale Players
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: Starship Flight 14 on Sept 28 was the first true orbital flight, deploying all 26 Starlink V3 satellites despite an engine shutdown on ascent; Starlink has 12.0M subscribers, Anthropic pays $1.25B a month through May 2029 and Google $920M a month from October; shares ~$159 (+7.4% Oct 2), ~$2.2T market cap.
rows.watch for: Q3 earnings, which start the clock on up to 1.3B lockup shares becoming tradable two full trading days later; falling Starlink ARPU ($66 vs $85) and $23.6B of H1 AI capex.

rows.angle: Completed a $1.94B at-the-market sale (~$66 average) to fund the $8B Iridium deal and dropped the $3.6B bridge loan; won a slot on the Space Force NITE-STAR vehicle (up to $981M pooled ceiling) and flew its 97th Electron, the 18th launch of 2026.
rows.watch for: FCC review of Iridium with closing guided to mid-2027, Neutron's maiden launch (13,000 kg to LEO) slipping, and a valuation above 40x annualized revenue on a $49.3M Q2 net loss.

rows.angle: Took $955M of the SDA's $1.75B award for 36 Golden Dome missile-tracking satellites (18 hypersonic and ballistic tracking variants), alongside the $4.7B PAC-3 propulsion award; also in the Defense sleeve.
rows.watch for: Conversion of awards into margin, with launches of this batch not expected until 2028; don't double-count with the Defense sleeve.

tiers.label: Growth / Speculative
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: BlueBirds 11-13 launched successfully and BlueBirds 14, 15 and 16 have shipped to Cape Canaveral; spacecraft production has reached BlueBird 50 and the CEO is pushing for broader FCC spectrum access.
rows.watch for: B.Riley cut to Neutral (target $65 from $85) on MNO uptake and pricing data still to come, plus Viasat and Space42's Equatys competing for the same direct-to-device market.

rows.angle: Delivered its 13th SiriusXM satellite and reports a record $1.8B backlog.
rows.watch for: Net insider selling of roughly $259M over 12 months and whether the backlog converts to recognized revenue.

rows.angle: Secured a German government contract worth up to $29M over five years and is scaling Pelican output with a new Berlin facility.
rows.watch for: Dependence on SpaceX rideshare capacity, which tightens by 2028, and founder stock sales.

rows.angle: One of 15 vendors on the Space Force NITE STAR IDIQ (ceiling over $980M) and still carrying a record ~$542M backlog; closed around $10.88 on Oct 2.
rows.watch for: NITE STAR has no guaranteed revenue, and the $1.15B of net insider selling over 12 months remains unexplained.

private_watchlist.name: Blue Origin
private_watchlist.note: New Glenn exploded during a static hot fire at LC-36 on May 28, destroying the transporter-erector at its only pad; CEO Dave Limp is still targeting another launch before the end of 2026, which looks ambitious for the repair work involved.

private_watchlist.name: Firefly Aerospace
private_watchlist.note: Signed a lunar AI-computing deal with Starcloud and opened a new cleanroom on Sept 22 to scale spacecraft production; Alpha Block 2's debut remains slated for Q4 2026.

private_watchlist.name: Stoke Space
private_watchlist.note: No fresh update this week beyond the $1B Series E (total raised $2.3B, ~$10B valuation); Nova Block 2, a 15-metric-ton fully reusable design, is still targeted for 2029.

bear_case.title: Capital intensity
bear_case.description: Rocket Lab just raised $1.94B of equity (~$66 a share) with a $49.3M quarterly net loss and could reach ~12% dilution after the Iridium close; AST SpaceMobile carries a $1.15B convertible plus ~$610M of quarterly capex; SpaceX itself spent $23.6B on AI capex in H1.

bear_case.title: Government concentration
bear_case.description: The SDA's $1.75B Tranche 3 award was split between L3Harris ($955M) and Sierra Space ($798M), and NITE-STAR is a pooled vehicle with no guaranteed revenue for any of its vendors; Golden Dome spending is large but spread thin across many bidders.

bear_case.title: SpaceX absorbs the value / lockups
bear_case.description: At ~$2.2T SpaceX is priced for flawless execution, Starlink ARPU is already falling, and up to 1.3B lockup shares can trade after Q3 earnings; its launch cost and cadence keep compressing everyone else's margins.

bear_case.title: Binary mission risk
bear_case.description: Flight 14 reached orbit but still lost an engine on ascent; Neutron's maiden launch is exposed to slipping into 2027; Blue Origin's only pad was wrecked in May; and a failure in any of these resets sector sentiment quickly.

catalysts.title: SpaceX +7.4% to ~$159 after a run of wins
catalysts.description: Starship Flight 14, NASA's Crew-13 launch and Alphabet's Project Suncatcher prototype all landed within a week; analysts' average target is $235.

catalysts.title: B.Riley cuts AST SpaceMobile to Neutral
catalysts.description: Target lowered to $65 from $85 on MNO pricing and subscriber uncertainty; BlueBirds 14-16 shipped to Cape Canaveral and shares were roughly flat at ~$57.

catalysts.title: Starship Flight 14 reaches orbit
catalysts.description: First true orbital flight, deploying all 26 Starlink V3 satellites despite an engine shutdown during ascent.

catalysts.title: Rocket Lab fully funds Iridium
catalysts.description: $1.94B at-the-market sale at ~$66 average, bridge loan terminated, plus a NITE-STAR slot and the 97th Electron launch; closing guided to mid-2027.

catalysts.title: Smaller names pick up contracts
catalysts.description: Planet Labs won a German contract worth up to $29M over five years and Intuitive Machines delivered its 13th SiriusXM satellite.

catalysts.title: SpaceX Q3 earnings and lockup release
catalysts.description: Up to 1.3B shares become tradable two full trading days after the release (date not yet confirmed); Blue Origin targets New Glenn's return to flight before year-end.

etfs.name: Procure Space
etfs.summary: Pure-play, revenue-weighted (RKLB, PL, ASTS among top holdings); up roughly 23% over the trailing 12 months as last reported Sept 28, with no fresh figure this week.

etfs.name: ARK Space Exploration
etfs.summary: Actively managed with broader tech adjacency; up roughly 18% trailing 12 months as last reported, and ARK has been adding RKLB.

etfs.name: SPDR Kensho Final Frontiers
etfs.summary: Equal-weight space, defense and deep-sea blend; up roughly 42% trailing 12 months as last reported, the strongest of the three.

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: Rocket Lab
positions.note: Fully funded the $8B Iridium deal with a $1.94B at-the-market sale (~$66 average, ~5% dilution) and killed the $3.6B bridge loan, but at ~$69 it trades above 40x annualized revenue with a $49.3M Q2 net loss, so the weight holds rather than grows.

positions.name: L3Harris
positions.note: Won $955M of the SDA's $1.75B Tranche 3 tracking-layer award (18 satellites) on top of the $4.7B PAC-3 propulsion award, so the backlog thesis is intact even with no new catalyst this week; also sits in the Defense sleeve, so don't double-count it.

positions.name: AST SpaceMobile
positions.note: B.Riley cut it to Neutral and slashed its target to $65 from $85 (stock ~$57) on MNO pricing and subscriber uncertainty plus rivals like Viasat and Space42's Equatys, even as BlueBirds 14-16 shipped to Cape Canaveral; weight trimmed, stance held.

positions.name: Intuitive Machines
positions.note: Delivered its 13th SiriusXM satellite and still reports a record $1.8B backlog, but heavy net insider selling (~$259M over 12 months) and unproven backlog conversion keep it small.

positions.name: Planet Labs
positions.note: Added a German government contract worth up to $29M over five years (+3% on the week), a real but small proof point for a business still dependent on SpaceX rideshare capacity.

positions.name: SpaceX
positions.note: Starship Flight 14 finally reached orbit Sept 28 with all 26 Starlink V3 satellites and shares jumped 7.4% to ~$159 on Oct 2, but a ~$2.2T market cap, Starlink ARPU down to $66 from $85 and up to 1.3B lockup shares unlocking after Q3 earnings keep it on Watch; UK investors wanting indirect exposure can use Scottish Mortgage (SMT, covered on the Baillie Gifford page).

positions.name: Redwire
positions.note: Closed around $10.88 on Oct 2 with the NITE STAR IDIQ slot still carrying no guaranteed revenue and the $1.15B of net insider selling over 12 months still unexplained, so nothing this week earns it a place in the sleeve.

positions.name: Iridium Communications
positions.note: Shareholders already approved the Rocket Lab deal (99.6% of votes), leaving only FCC review before a mid-2027 close, so the standalone stock is just a spread on RKLB's share price and RKLB is the cleaner way to hold the view.
